words: Challenge Point should generate the simplest coherent learning environment that provides meaningful, recurring opportunities to encounter the intended Game Problem.
Please treat minimum necessary complexity as a design preference to evaluate, not a numerical quota or a restriction on valid combinations.
If both teams understand the rules and genuinely attempt to win, do their available opportunities and incentives make the intended learning problem likely to emerge?
This is not about compelling the defenders to press or requiring a prescribed tactical solution.
I consider this dual-team incentive coherence a necessary part of evaluating the A02 design.
Present the revised activity with concise coach-facing instructions and clear labels distinguishing approved, candidate, proposed and illustrative elements.
Please continue protecting A01 and the live application.
No changes to the A02 pathway or unapproved scoring arrangements are authorized for release.
The package should stop when a coherent A02 candidate is ready for ecological review or when a genuinely new knowledge decision prevents further progress.
Please proceed with the bounded A02 comparison and revision under these conditions.
However, because the pressing team knows this condition, it may benefit from avoiding coordinated pressure and thereby preventing its opponent from becoming eligible to score.
I do not want a broad audit, new architectural layer, or expansion into advanced engagement and adaptive feedback.
rulings.file: christian-2026-11-13-a02-revision-package.txt (Christian's reply received 13 November 2026, headings 1, 2 and 11, the foundational principle, the critical finding and the next development package)

words: I am comfortable retaining asymmetric escaping and pressing roles as a review-level candidate, including exchanging roles between blocks.
However, I am not yet approving the particular marked-line placement, expansive escaping-team target zone or pressing-team scoring arrangement as canonical knowledge.
First, the large target zone may make successful scoring possible through long-ball bypasses without the attacking team genuinely solving an established coordinated press.
Second, the pressing team's only scoring option—dribbling over the opponent's end line—may unnecessarily narrow its attacking solutions.
Third, because of the proposed restart, the escaping team may be able to avoid an unfavorable turnover by putting the ball over its own end line.
I'd like the next package to examine whether a more coherent relationship between defensive rewards, attacking targets and possession consequences would better support the learning intention.
These are examples from experience and current exploration, not automatically approved A02 scoring rules or verified superiority claims.
rulings.file: christian-2026-11-13-a02-revision-package.txt (Christian's reply received 13 November 2026, heading 3, Questions 1 and 2: Roles, Line, Targets and Defensive Scoring)

words: For now, no offside may remain an isolated review assumption, but I am not approving it as a general A02 rule.
The important concern is whether players can position themselves beyond the pressure and repeatedly score through long passes without meaningfully encountering the intended game problem.
However, I don't want to fix this automatically by introducing a rule that dictates where attacking players must stand.
Please evaluate the problem within the proposed game and identify the smallest representative solution, including whether a Law 11 decision is actually necessary for the chosen game structure.
rulings.file: christian-2026-11-13-a02-revision-package.txt (Christian's reply received 13 November 2026, heading 5, Question 3: Offside)

words: I approve the underlying principle that coordinated pressure must genuinely be encountered and that it need not remain intact after the attacking team has escaped it.
A qualifying High Press Escape sequence should not automatically be equated with the entire attacking possession.
The important relationship is between encountering established coordinated pressure and subsequently escaping it while preserving attacking continuity.
Facing coordinated pressure earlier in possession should not automatically qualify an unrelated later scoring event.
Please preserve that distinction without introducing unnecessary phase machinery or elaborate referee-like conditions for coaches.
I would also hold the four High Press Escape coach-facing scoring rules until we settle the game structure and review the resulting wording.
"Pressing team" is an acceptable role description.
I would avoid instructions such as "set to press together" if they become prescriptions for defensive behavior rather than descriptions of a representative starting condition.
Please use the existing approved High Press Escape coach translation wherever appropriate rather than independently adding lengthy explanations.
The coach should understand the activity quickly without needing to understand the system's internal reasoning.
I would prefer concise Setup, Rules, Scoring and Learning Explanation sections, with technical qualifications kept in the underlying representation where possible.
Clarity is more important than achieving an arbitrary word count, but the current 326-word review presentation can be simplified.
rulings.file: christian-2026-11-13-a02-revision-package.txt (Christian's reply received 13 November 2026, heading 6, Questions 4 and 5: Coach Wording and Qualifying Sequences)

words: I would not approve an automatic restart to the escaping team after every end-line ball, regardless of who last touched it.
That can weaken possession consequences and potentially reward deliberate clearances or avoidance of pressure.
My preference remains to preserve meaningful possession consequences and reasonable coach discretion.

A representative coach-managed restart can be useful when the activity needs to recreate the relevant pressure situation, but it should not automatically become the only permitted way a qualifying sequence begins.
Please propose a simple, practical restart arrangement compatible with the selected scoring structure and intended game problem.
We shouldn't spend another development cycle optimizing every possible restart case.
We need something coherent, representative and manageable.
rulings.file: christian-2026-11-13-a02-revision-package.txt (Christian's reply received 13 November 2026, heading 7, Question 6: Restarts)
